To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

brief Na+ deprivation is enough to alter patterns of NaCl ingestion, to decrease gustatory responses to the amiloride-insensitive component of the chorda-tympani nerve (the component that responds to Na+), and to reduce CT responses to the amilioride-sensitive component of CT.
dietary Na+ deprivation reduces CT responses to Na+ and increases the consumption of concentrated NaCl solutions, and that these changes occur rapidly, within 2 days of sodium deprivation.

2 days of sodium deprivation is sufficient to increase the intake of NaCl, reduce the gustatory responses to all concentrations of NaCl, and reduce the amiloride sensitivity of the chordatympani nerve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural and behavioral mechanisms underlying the control of sodium intake in rats.
the mechanisms underlying the behavioral and gustatory responses to dietary Na+ deprivation.
the neural and behavioral mechanisms that mediate the ingestive and metabolic responses to dietary sodium deprivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dietary Na+ deprivation rapidly changes the behavioral responses to NaCl, which is consistent with the rapid onset of the behavioral response to NaCl, while CT responses to Na+ are reduced more slowly, which may be necessary for the behavioral response to be fully expressed.
2 days of salt-deprivation is sufficient to alter the pattern of ingestion of concentrated salt, and that the amiloride sensitive component of the CT is reduced during salt-deprivation.
the behavioral and electrophysiology responses to taste change within 24 h of Na+ deprivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gustatory system responds to dietary Na+ deprivation in a manner similar to the renal system.
dietary Na+ deprivation rapidly alters both gustatory and behavioral responses to NaCl.
the gustatory system is a critical component of the adaptive response to dietary Na+ deprivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the taste system is highly sensitive to changes in dietary Na+ and that these changes may contribute to the behavioral and hormonal responses to Na+ deprivation.
changes in taste sensitivity occur within 48 h after Na+ deprivation, and these changes may play an important role in the behavioral response to Na+ deprivation.
dietary Na+ deprivation can have a significant impact on gustatory responses within a few days of onset, and this is likely due to a reduction in amiloride-sensitive responses to NaCl.
